records.name: Al-Aqsa Islamic Society
records.summary: A mosque and community center in Kensington with a Youth Club, an Interfaith program and an Outreach program. The society has been operating since 1989.
records.what_you_do: The site names an Interfaith program, an Outreach program and a Youth Club but gives no details. Call the office to ask how to join each one and whether visitors are welcome at prayer.

schedule.text: The site has a prayer times heading but no times in the text we could read. The events calendar and announcements had no items.

first_step.how: Call (215) 765-2743 or use the contact form on the site
first_step.basis: The site names programs but gives no dates, costs or sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: Listed as a Religious Leaders Council member on Interfaith Philadelphia's page. The CAIR listing also shows a full-time school, a Saturday school, social events and burial services, but the site does not confirm these, so they are left out. Status is probably_active because the site works but has no dated items.

records.name: Germantown Masjid (Masjid as-Sunnah an-Nabawiyyah)
records.summary: A mosque on Germantown Avenue that runs free classes from Wednesday to Sunday, open to brothers and sisters. It also has an academy, an enrichment program and a weekly outreach booth downtown.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free class on any day from Wednesday to Sunday, or ask about the academy and the enrichment program. The mosque also runs an outreach booth in Downtown Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Free classes Wednesday to Sunday, taught by qualified students of knowledge. Class times are on a separate schedule page that could not be read. Office hours are 10 am to sunset every day.

first_step.how: Go to a class, or call 267-900-5371 to ask about the schedule
first_step.basis: Classes are free and open to brothers and sisters, and the site has material for new Muslims, but it does not say how a newcomer should start.

records.notes: The home page shows prayer times for Sunday, 4 October 2026, which is the newest evidence. Its news items date from 2021 and 2022. CAIR lists 4944 Germantown Ave and a different phone number, so the mosque's own site is used. Friday prayer times are not shown. The site says the outreach booths and seminar audio are open, but does not say whether the other programs are.

records.name: Masjidullah
records.summary: A mosque on Limekiln Pike with Friday prayer and programs for families. The site also lists health and human services and Ramadan programs, and links to a child care center and a learning institute on their own sites.
records.what_you_do: Attend Friday prayer at 1:15 pm, sign up to volunteer through the site, or ask the office about the child care center and the New Medina Institute.

schedule.text: Friday prayer service at 1:15 pm. Other class and program times are not on the site.

first_step.how: Call the office at 215-621-7800 or email inquiries@masjidullah.org. Membership and volunteer sign-up forms are on the site.
first_step.basis: The site asks people to sign up for membership or volunteering, and it does not say whether visitors are welcome at Friday prayer.

records.notes: The events page shows only flyer images with no readable dates. The footer's 2017 copyright is not used as evidence. CAIR gives a different phone number (215-424-8022), which is not used. The child care center and New Medina Institute have their own sites, which were not read.

records.name: Masjid al-Jamia
records.summary: A masjid in West Philadelphia that teaches Quran recitation with tajweed, tafsir, hadith and practical fiqh, and runs a children's Islamic school. It also has youth programs and weekly tafsir and hadith circles.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly tafsir or hadith circle, enroll children in the Islamic school, or come to a family event with talks, halal food stalls and children's activities. The site gives no date for the family event.

schedule.text: Weekly tafsir and hadith circles, and Quran classes. Prayer times are shown as images that could not be read. No class days or times are in readable text.

first_step.how: Call (267) 275-8087 or use the contact form on the site
first_step.basis: Classes are said to be open to all ages, and the site lists a phone number and a contact form, but it does not say how to register or whether classes cost money.

records.notes: The neighborhood family event has no date or year on the site. The lecture videos on YouTube are undated. The announcements and event calendar pages had no items in the text we could read. CAIR lists a ZIP code that the site does not give, so no ZIP is recorded.

records.name: Masjid Mujahideen
records.summary: A masjid on South 60th Street with social services, a Jawala Scouts program for young people, and a youth fundraising gala.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, take part in the social services, join the Jawala Scouts, or buy a ticket to a community event. The site invites people to volunteer, take part or donate.

schedule.text: No regular times are listed. The events page says community events are coming but names none. A youth fundraising gala was held on December 27, 2024.

cost.text: Gala tickets were sold through a link that is not in the text; other costs not stated

first_step.how: Call (215) 471-7073 or email the address shown on the site
first_step.basis: The page invites volunteers and donors but lists no class times or sign-up steps.

records.notes: The page displays admin@masjidmujahideen.org, but its mail link goes to a different Gmail address. Confirm which one works before publishing. The gala is the only dated item. Its 2024 date is about 22 months old, so status is probably_active.

records.name: Center City Mosque
records.summary: A small mosque on Walnut Street that holds daily prayers, Friday prayers and weekly Quran circles for children, youth and adults. It also holds Ramadan iftar gatherings and Eid prayers.
records.what_you_do: Come to the second Friday prayer, which is open to brothers and sisters, or ask about the Quran circles. Special programs include Ramadan iftar gatherings, Eid prayers and community service projects.

schedule.text: Friday prayer: first session 1:10 to 1:35 pm for brothers only, second session 1:50 to 2:15 pm for brothers and sisters. Daily prayer times are on the home page. Quran circles meet weekly but have no posted time.

cost.text: No fee listed; the mosque asks for donations to expand its space

first_step.how: Come to the second Friday prayer, or call 267-817-4433 or email centercitymosque@gmail.com for class times
first_step.basis: Friday prayer is open to brothers and sisters, and the phone and email are listed, but the site has no newcomer program.

records.notes: The home page shows its current date as Wednesday, October 7, 2026, which is the newest evidence. Class and event pages give no dates or years. CAIR lists 1215 Clover St, which is not used because the mosque's own site gives 1328 Walnut St. The site did not say whether the iftar and Eid gatherings are open to visitors. A third Jumuah time appears in a widget but not in the text, so it is not recorded.

records.name: Masjid Quba (Quba Institute)
records.summary: A masjid that says it is Philadelphia's oldest, established in 1938. It offers Jumu'ah prayer, classes, a food pantry, counseling and community outings, and membership dues apply for the full set of benefits.
records.what_you_do: Members get congregational prayers and worship services, a free yearly Islamic studies intensive and discounts on courses. The site also lists classes, a food pantry, counseling and community outings.

schedule.text: Jumu'ah prayer is listed as a service, but its time is not shown in the text we could read. Class times are not given.

cost.text: Membership: $35 a month for an individual, $50 a month for a family of up to five, $20 a month for seniors, fixed income people and students

first_step.how: Read the membership page or call 215-473-8589 ext 100
first_step.basis: Membership dues come before the full benefits, and the site does not say whether non-members can attend Jumu'ah or classes.

records.notes: The masjid page heading reads 2024 to 2025 with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is set. The institute's site lists a day school, a seminary and a masjid section, but those pages were not read. The masjid's own pages show no street address, so the institute address is used. Interfaith's Religious Leaders Council lists this masjid under the name Quba Masjid. The site footer shows a 2035 copyright, which is not used.

records.name: United Muslim Masjid
records.summary: A masjid in South Philadelphia, founded in 1994, with weekly Islamic classes on Tuesdays and Fridays after Isha prayer. The Friday class is streamed live online.
records.what_you_do: Join the Tuesday class on the inner dimensions of prayer, or the Friday class, which you can attend online. The site also lists volunteer sign-up, Zakat al-Fitr and a monthly giving program.

schedule.text: Tuesday class and Friday class, both after Isha prayer. The Friday class is live online. Prayer times and the khateeb schedule are posted as images. The first class resumes in January, with no year given.

locations.label: UMIC (second location named on the site)

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page, or join the Friday class online
first_step.basis: Classes are listed with days and times and the site has a contact page, but it does not say whether beginners are welcome.

records.notes: The site footer shows 2025, which is not used as evidence. Prayer times and the khateeb schedule are images and were not read. The Telegram channel has no link on the site, so it is not recorded. Phone and email come from the CAIR listing because the site's contact page did not show them. The site says the masjid was established on October 11, 1994.

records.name: Muslim Youth Center of Philadelphia (MYCP)
records.summary: A youth and community center at 11080 Knights Road, run by the Muslim Society of Delaware Valley. It has Friday prayer, Quran reading sessions, a teen circle and a sisters' wellness series.
records.what_you_do: Pray Jumu'ah on Fridays, join a Quran reading session or a Teen Seekers circle, or come to the Muslim Youth Circle or the sisters' wellness series. The center also lists a weekend learning program, summer camp and volunteering.

schedule.text: October 2026 calendar. Jumu'ah prayer on Fridays at 1:15 to 2 pm (Oct 2, 9, 16, 23, 30). Quran reading and recitation 5 to 7 pm on many days. Teen Seekers 2 to 5 pm and Adult Quran Reading Circle 4:30 to 6:30 pm on Sundays (Oct 4, 11, 18, 25). Muslim Youth Circle 6 to 8 pm (Oct 3). Sisters' Wellness Series 3 to 5 pm (Oct 10).

first_step.how: Call (215) 437-9987 or email mycpweekendlearning@gmail.com. The imam's office hours, 4 to 6 pm on the listed Fridays, are walk in or by email appointment.
first_step.basis: The calendar gives times and walk in office hours are listed, but the site does not describe a newcomer program or say who may attend each event.

records.notes: The CAIR listing gives mycphiladelphia.com, which does not resolve, so this record uses the Muslim Society of Delaware Valley site, which runs the center. Footer details on the MSDV home page are placeholders and were not used. Times come from the calendar entries on the MYCP page. Eligibility for each event is not stated. The society's other center, the Islamic Cultural Center of Willow Grove, is outside the city and is not recorded.

records.name: Mahdieh
records.summary: A nonprofit Islamic educational center on Haverford Avenue, founded in 2000, that serves Iranian American Muslims. Its Friday night program includes prayers, a lecture and a shared dinner.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Friday night program, which starts at 7 pm with prayers, a lecture and dinner. The imam is available in person on Fridays and on special occasions.

schedule.text: The Friday night program starts at 7 pm with the call to prayer and the Maghrib and Isha prayers, then a lecture and dinner. Religious observance dates are posted as all day events with month and day only.

cost.text: Not stated; the center takes donations through PayPal

first_step.how: Come to the Friday night program, or email info@mahdieh.org
first_step.basis: The site describes the Friday program but does not say how a newcomer should start or whether visitors are welcome.

records.notes: The prayer-time page shows Thursday, 8 October 2026, which is the newest evidence. The event calendar shows month and day only, so no event year is recorded. The imam's personal phone number and email on the site are not recorded; the phone number above comes from the CAIR listing. The site does not say whether non-members are welcome at the Friday program.

records.name: Association of Islamic Charitable Projects (AICP)
records.summary: A nonprofit at 4431 Walnut Street that runs TIES Islamic schools, full time on weekdays and part time on weekends, and publishes free Islamic articles and audio.
records.what_you_do: Read the free articles and audio, look into the weekday full time or weekend part time schools, or donate. The site does not list volunteer programs.

schedule.text: Weekday full time and weekend part time schools. Days and times are on separate school pages that were not read. Dated events on the site have no years.

first_step.how: Call 215-387-8888 or read the TIES contacts page
first_step.basis: The site lists schools but not enrollment steps, dates or costs.

records.notes: The homepage shows a header date of Thursday, 8 October 2026. That is treated as page display, not as event evidence. The site lists a phone number with a 714 area code, which differs from the CAIR listing (215-387-8888). The CAIR number is used. The site does not say whether schools or events are open to non-members.

records.name: Bawa Muhaiyaddeen Fellowship
records.summary: A Sufi-inspired fellowship on Overbrook Avenue that runs a mosque named for Shaikh M. R. Bawa Muhaiyaddeen, with dhikr sessions and adult classes.
records.what_you_do: Ask about the dhikr sessions and adult classes. The fellowship's own site could not be read, so check the current schedule by phone or email.

schedule.text: Dhikr sessions and adult classes are listed in a directory. Days and times could not be read.

first_step.basis: Only a directory listing could be read, so the way in and the schedule are not confirmed.

Bawa Muhaiyaddeen as a member. Status is unknown. Hold before publishing if a reviewer cannot confirm the group is running. The CAIR listing gives dhikr and adult classes but no times.

records.name: Chenrezig Tibetan Buddhist Center
records.summary: A Tibetan Buddhist center on North Marshall Street with a Sunday sangha that includes silent meditation and a dharma talk, in person and on Zoom. It also runs an online Thursday study group.
records.what_you_do: Join the Sunday sangha, with silent meditation from 9 to 9:45 am and teaching from 10 am, in person or online. The site says the sangha is recommended for beginners. The Thursday online study group is open to anyone who wants to join at any time.

schedule.text: Sunday sangha 10 to 11:30 am, with silent meditation from 9 to 9:45 am, in person and on Zoom. Thursday online study group at 7 pm Eastern.

cost.text: Suggested donation of $5 for students and $10 for adults. Included for monthly members.

first_step.how: Come in person, or join on Zoom using the link on the site. Email info@tibetanbuddhist.org with questions.
first_step.basis: The Sunday sangha is recommended for beginners, and the site gives both an in person address and an online link.

records.notes: Status follows the newest dated evidence rule. The newest dated item is a March 8, 2024 COVID mask notice on the Thursday page, and the sand mandala event is from 2022. The Sunday and Thursday schedules are undated and read as current, so confirm with the center by email before publishing. Zoom links and meeting codes are not recorded. The site does not show a phone number.

records.name: Kadampa Meditation Center Philadelphia
records.summary: A Buddhist meditation center on North 2nd Street with weekly classes on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, plus a monthly prayers for world peace session on the first Friday.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly meditation class, come to the monthly prayers for world peace (free), or sign up for the half day course listed on the site. Most classes cost $15 and the Thursday morning class costs $5, and membership covers both.

schedule.text: Sunday morning meditation 10:30 to 11:45 am. Monday Rest and Reflect 7 to 8 pm. The Power to Change on Wednesdays 7 to 8 pm. Thursday morning meditation 8 to 8:30 am. Prayers for World Peace on the first Friday of the month, 7 to 8 pm. Class dates on the site are written without a year.

cost.text: $15 for most weekly classes and $5 for Thursday morning meditation, both included in membership. Prayers for World Peace is free.

first_step.how: Call 267-702-3817 (voicemail, they call back) or use the contact form on the site
first_step.basis: Each class is listed as open to everyone with no experience needed, and the center says everyone is always welcome.

records.notes: The Jivaka listing gives 1102 Pine St, which is not used because the center's own site gives 47 N. 2nd Street. Upcoming course: The Peace of Wisdom, Saturday, Oct 17, 10:30 am to 1:30 pm, $20. The page gives no year for that date. The 2022 footer is not used as evidence. Ardmore and Collingswood classes on the same site are outside the city and are not recorded.

notes: Searches used: 3 of 3 (mosque list, Hindu and Sikh list, Buddhist list). Fetches used: 58 of 60. TARGET MISSED: 14 publishable records, not 15. HINDU AND SIKH GAP: no Hindu temple (mandir) or Sikh gurdwara inside the City of Philadelphia could be verified in this run, so none are recorded. The Hindu and Sikh searches turned up only: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir in Levittown (Bucks County, outside the city, so dropped); HARI Temple in New Cumberland (central PA, dropped); a 2023 Penn student langar event (a student group, not a gurdwara, dropped); and a Guru Nanak Sikh Temple listing whose page was refused. Recommend a fresh search pass for these two faiths, using mandir and gurdwara lists for Philadelphia, before the wave closes. INTERFAITH PHILADELPHIA: its main pages name no mosques, temples or gurdwaras as members. Its Religious Leaders Council page names Al-Aqsa Islamic Society, Quba Masjid, the Bawa Muhaiyaddeen mosque and South Philadelphia Shtiebel (Jewish). Its Everyday Faith: Hinduism event (Oct 22, 2026, virtual, sliding scale $25 to $125) is a paid Interfaith workshop, not a temple program, so it is not recorded. MAIN LIST: the CAIR Pennsylvania directory shows 52 Philadelphia mosque entries. Most records come from that list plus each group's own site. BUDDHIST: only Chenrezig and Kadampa Meditation Center had usable current sites. The Jivaka directory lists about ten more Philadelphia Buddhist places. Most have last visit dates from 2013 to 2019 and no own website, so they are in leads_only, not records. Chua Phat Quang was dropped because its listing says the location is closed or moved. STATUS RULES: Chenrezig is set to dormant by the newest dated item (a March 8, 2024 mask notice), even though its Sunday and Thursday schedules read as current. Confirm before publishing. Undated working sites are probably_active. Quba's newest date is a 2024 to 2025 heading with no month, so no last_sign_of_life is set. DROPPED WEBSITES: Masjid Muhammad (its site holds only youth group articles, no masjid details); Masjid Muqbil (domain for sale); Al-Rashideen Islamic Center (parked domain); NEICC (neicc.net redirects to a Brooklyn and New Jersey center, not the Northeast Philadelphia Islamic Center); Nur uz-Zamaan Institute (Pittsburgh, does not name the Paschall Ave masjid). OPEN TO VISITORS: many sites do not say whether programs are open to non-members. Worship congregations are set to open_to public, which is flagged for review. Quba is set to members because its site lists membership dues for the masjid's benefits. CONTACTS: Mahdieh's site shows the imam's personal phone and email, which are not recorded. Germantown Masjid, Masjidullah, Center City Mosque and AICP each show a different phone or address in CAIR than on their own sites; the own site value is used in each case. MYCP's own domain does not resolve, so the record uses msdvpa.org, which runs the center. Masjid Mujahideen's site shows an admin email, but its mail link goes elsewhere; the shown address is used. NOT YET REACHABLE: Masjid Abdullah Bin Baaz (TLS error) and Northeast Philadelphia Islamic Center (DNS). Out of city and not recorded: Islamic Cultural Center of Willow Grove (MSDV's other center), Won Buddhism (Glenside), Philadelphia Meditation Center (Havertown), Soji Zen Center (Lansdowne).
